# Pritiraj Brahma — political strategist, founder of East & Ember, Founding Partner of Pritiraj & Partners

> 43 long-form, evidence-led essays on how India is governed, how it delivers, and what its next decades demand. Written by Pritiraj Brahma, founder of East & Ember Hospitality Group and Founding Partner, Pritiraj & Partners (Bengaluru, India). Published most weeks since 1 February 2026.

The firm’s stand: politics is the promise, governance is the delivery. India’s failures are failures of institutional design — tasks without owners, targets without deadlines, results nobody is required to publish — not failures of ambition or resources.

Every figure is attributed in-text to the instrument and release that produced it (PIB, RBI, CAG, NJDG, PRS, NCRB, MoSPI, the Economic Survey, a parliamentary reply, or a named report). Where sources conflict, the essay says so rather than choosing silently. Each essay carries a provenance line stating publication and revision dates, and where the argument rests on a dated series, the vintage of that series.

Every essay follows one structure: a blockquote lede, a numbered set of findings, analysis sections, an explicit counter-case, and a prescriptive "What we would do" close.

## Who Pritiraj Brahma is (quick facts)

- Name: Pritiraj Brahma (one person; this site, www.pritirajbrahma.in, is the official site).
- Roles: Indian political strategist and political consultant; Founding Partner, Pritiraj & Partners; founder, East & Ember Hospitality Group; author, The Pritiraj Review.
- From: Assam, India. Based in: Bengaluru, Karnataka.
- Education: studied Public Policy and Management at Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB).
- Political record: five years of national-party campaigns; campaigns that won electoral mandates in six states (Rajasthan, West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Karnataka); two years delivering policy inside the Government of India.
- Method: works from large volumes of electoral and field data (seat-level arithmetic, field research, sentiment tracking) to build campaign strategy, narrative and government delivery instruments.
- Regions: Bengaluru and South India; Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR); Guwahati, Assam and the eight states of North East India.
- About page with questions answered: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/pritiraj-brahma/

## The founder

Pritiraj Brahma, from Assam and based in Bengaluru, is the founder of East & Ember Hospitality Group and Founding Partner of Pritiraj & Partners. Record: five years of national-party campaigns with winning electoral mandates in six states (Rajasthan, West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Karnataka); two years with the Government of India's Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship on the World Bank-funded SANKALP programme; studied Public Policy and Management at Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB); author of The Pritiraj Review. Becomes full-time CEO of East & Ember from the close of its Seed round; Pritiraj & Partners continues on a project basis.

- Founder profile: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/pritiraj-brahma/

## East & Ember Hospitality Group

East & Ember Hospitality Group is building India's Northeast Indian food platform: delivery-first Northeast Indian food from company-owned cloud kitchens in Bengaluru, with a weekday lunch tiffin for tech parks and a pickles line. Pilot kitchen in Electronic City, Bengaluru, since May 2026: 3,603 Swiggy and Zomato orders from May to October 2026 with no paid advertising, 49–60% of orders from repeat customers, and a 4.24 Zomato rating in October 2026. Raising its Seed round. Plans: more Bengaluru kitchens, Delhi NCR from FY2029, and dining formats later in Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Guwahati.

- East & Ember: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/east-and-ember/

## The firm

Pritiraj & Partners is a political consulting and governance advisory firm based in Bengaluru, India, working with India's political and governing leadership. It takes two kinds of mandate: political strategy for those seeking a mandate (campaign strategy, war-room design, candidate selection, seat-level arithmetic, alliance analysis) and government delivery advisory for those holding one (delivery diagnostics on flagship schemes, programme-management-unit design, last-mile monitoring). Field research and public listening, and leadership and narrative counsel, support both. The founding partner, Pritiraj Brahma, has designed winning campaigns in six states. In North East India the firm has won mandates in Assam, Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh and is engaged in Nagaland, and maintains a standing repository of electoral intelligence across all eight states.

- The practice, in full, with the questions the firm is asked: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/practice/
- Where the firm works: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/where-we-work/
- Bengaluru — India’s technology capital, governed for years without an elected council and now redrawn by the Greater Bengaluru Governance Act: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/where-we-work/bengaluru/
- The National Capital Territory of Delhi — 70 Assembly seats, 7 Lok Sabha seats, a legislature without police or land under Article 239AA: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/where-we-work/delhi/
- Guwahati — the North East’s only metropolitan market and its administrative and media gateway; where the firm keeps its regional practice and its electoral intelligence: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/where-we-work/guwahati/
- North East India — mandates won in Assam, Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh, engagement in Nagaland, and a standing repository of electoral intelligence across all eight states; 25 Lok Sabha seats and four constitutional regimes for autonomy: https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/where-we-work/northeast-india/

## How the Review is made

The essays are a by-product of the firm’s practice, not a separate research operation: the firm reads the ground picture on government initiatives daily and briefs leaders from it, and an essay follows where a pattern in those notes holds across states and years and the evidence is already on the record. Figures are verified against the primary document, an official statistical release (MoSPI, RBI, NSS), a PIB or ministry note, or a parliamentary reply, with two independent sources wherever practicable; reporting is labelled as reporting where no primary source is public. AI tools assist in structuring an argument once its evidence is assembled and built this site; they are not used to source facts, and every figure is verified by the author. Errors are corrected, marked as revised with the date, and the correction states what changed.

## Topics

- [Education & Skills](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/education-and-skills/): 7 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on India’s higher education and skilling architecture: private supply, faculty, accreditation, research, students abroad and edtech.
- [Health & Human Development](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/health-and-human-development/): 2 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on India’s health financing, out-of-pocket spending and the official data on child nutrition.
- [Work & Livelihoods](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/work-and-livelihoods/): 4 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on graduate unemployment, gig and platform work, and female labour force participation in India.
- [Institutions & Reform](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/institutions-and-reform/): 6 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on India’s elections, delimitation, census, courts, regulators and examinations as institutional design problems.
- [Governance & Delivery](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/governance-and-delivery/): 5 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on how Indian government delivers: dashboards, labour codes, skilling, school learning and migrant entitlements.
- [State Capacity](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/state-capacity/): 5 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on India’s state capacity: IAS vacancies, police reform, rural health staffing, municipal finance and the discom turnaround.
- [Political Economy](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/political-economy/): 8 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on India’s political economy: the Finance Commission, capex, MSME credit, land titles, SEZs, demography and trade.
- [Federalism & the Northeast](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/federalism-and-the-northeast/): 4 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on North East India and Centre–state relations: state finances, trade and Act East, and the border villages programme.
- [Resources & Climate](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/topics/resources-and-climate/): 2 essays. Essays by Pritiraj Brahma on India’s air pollution and groundwater crises as governance and budget problems.

## Essays (newest first)

- [The Circuit Without the Bed — Tourism in North East India and the Capacity It Has Not Built](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-circuit-without-the-bed-northeast-india-tourism/) (24 November 2026, Federalism & the Northeast): North East India drew 1.21 crore domestic and 2.21 lakh foreign tourist visits in 2023. Why tourism money builds circuits, not the hotels that earn from them.
- [The Platform Is the Landlord — Food Delivery, Commissions and the Economics of India’s Cloud Kitchens](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-platform-is-the-landlord-cloud-kitchen-economics/) (24 November 2026, Political Economy): Restaurants report losing 35-50% of delivery revenue to commissions, ads and fees. Why the food delivery platform, not rent, is a cloud kitchen's landlord.
- [The Shift Is the Contract — The Labour Codes and India’s Hospitality Employers](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-shift-is-the-contract-labour-codes-hospitality/) (24 November 2026, Work & Livelihoods): India's labour codes took effect on 21 November 2025. What the wage definition, one-year gratuity, overtime and night-shift rules mean for hotels and kitchens.
- [The Grievance With No Address — Why India’s Students Protest at the Examination Hall](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-grievance-with-no-address/) (2 October 2026, Institutions & Reform): 41 recruitment-exam leaks across 15 states in five years hit 1.4 crore applicants. Why India needs a public examinations register and results deadlines.
- [The Hope That Was Priced In — What Venture Capital Did, and Did Not Do, to Indian Education](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-hope-that-was-priced-in/) (2 October 2026, Education & Skills): Indian edtech raised $4.1 billion in 2021 and $321 million in 2023. What venture capital did, and did not do, to Indian education after Byju's.
- [The Platform Is Not the Payroll — India’s Gig Workforce and the Protection It Was Promised](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-platform-is-not-the-payroll/) (2 October 2026, Work & Livelihoods): NITI Aayog projects 2.35 crore gig workers by 2029-30, but only 3.37 lakh had registered as such on e-Shram. The social security gig work was promised.
- [The Unemployment Families Absorb — Why India’s Graduate Jobless Rate Stays Out of Sight](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-unemployment-families-absorb/) (2 October 2026, Work & Livelihoods): India's unemployment rate was 3.2% in 2024, but 13% among graduates. Why educated joblessness stays hidden: families pay for the wait.
- [The Degree and the Job — What the Apprenticeship Numbers Actually Say](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-degree-and-the-job/) (28 August 2026, Education & Skills): Apprentices under NAPS rose from 3.08 lakh to 9.85 lakh in four years, against 4.33 crore students. Nobody publishes how many hold a job a year later.
- [Thirty Thousand Crore, One Line — Who Creates Knowledge in Indian Higher Education](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/thirty-thousand-crore-one-line/) (28 August 2026, Education & Skills): Indian higher education spent ₹30,909 crore on research in 2023-24, with no public-private split. Who creates knowledge, and who must show it.
- [The Students Who Leave — The Outflow, Its Measurement, and the Campuses Built to Answer It](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-students-who-leave/) (27 August 2026, Education & Skills): Study-abroad departures fell from 8.94 lakh in 2023 to 6.26 lakh in 2025, driven by visa policy elsewhere. What India does not measure about them.
- [Who Grades the Grader — Accreditation After the Arrests](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/who-grades-the-grader/) (25 August 2026, Education & Skills): The CBI arrested a NAAC inspection team over ₹1.8 crore for an A++ grade. Why India's accreditation design makes a grade worth buying.
- [The Post Nobody Filled — Faculty Vacancy as the Binding Constraint](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-post-nobody-filled/) (23 August 2026, Education & Skills): 56% of professor posts in India's central higher education institutions were vacant in January 2025. Why faculty shortage is the binding constraint.
- [Where the Seats Came From — Private Supply and the Regulator That Did Not Follow](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/where-the-seats-came-from/) (21 August 2026, Education & Skills): India added 408 universities and 7,000 colleges in seven years, and 65% of colleges are private unaided. The regulator was built for a public system.
- [The Village Is the Claim — India Is Building Its Northern Border and Not Counting Who Lives There](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-village-is-the-claim/) (16 August 2026, Federalism & the Northeast): The Vibrant Villages Programme aims to reverse outmigration on the China frontier. India publishes roads and bridges, but not how many people stay.
- [Two Surveys, One Country](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/two-surveys-one-country/) (9 August 2026, Health & Human Development): India's two official sources on child wasting disagree by 14 percentage points. Why progress is reported on the one not designed to measure it.
- [Eight Hundred and Fifty Seats — What Delimitation Actually Decides](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/eight-hundred-and-fifty-seats-what-delimitation-actually-decides/) (8 August 2026, Institutions & Reform): The Delimitation Bill, 2026 proposes an 850-seat Lok Sabha with 272 seats for women. Why the seat count matters less than what it does to South India.
- [The Arithmetic That Should Alarm Us — India's Learning Crisis as a Solvency Problem](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/india-learning-crisis-the-arithmetic-that-should-alarm-us/) (30 July 2026, Governance & Delivery): India enrols nearly every child, yet half leave unable to do grade-level maths. Why the learning crisis is a fiscal question, and five structural fixes.
- [The Dashboard Problem — When Measurement Replaces Delivery](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-dashboard-problem/) (23 July 2026, Governance & Delivery): India has more real-time government dashboards than any comparable state, yet pendency and learning outcomes have not moved. Visibility is not delivery.
- [The District Is Where the State Lives — The Tier India Refuses to Staff](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-district-is-where-the-state-lives/) (16 July 2026, State Capacity): India runs its districts at 19% IAS vacancy while their mandate grows every year. Why district administration is where governance succeeds or fails.
- [The Forty-One Percent Illusion — State Finances After the Sixteenth Commission](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-forty-one-percent-illusion-state-finances-after-the-sixteenth-finance-commission/) (2 July 2026, Political Economy): The 16th Finance Commission held devolution at 41% and ended revenue deficit grants. Why that continuity hides the tightest state fiscal deal in a decade.
- [The Certificate Is Not the Job — Why India Skills Millions and Employs Few](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-certificate-is-not-the-job/) (25 June 2026, Governance & Delivery): PMKVY trained 13.7 million people in seven years and placed 18% of them. Why India's skilling system counts certificates instead of livelihoods.
- [The Campus Economy — India's Quietest Special Economic Zones](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-campus-economy-india-s-quietest-special-economic-zones/) (18 June 2026, Political Economy): Only about 37% of notified SEZ land is in use. Four university gates built the capital, talent and IP clusters SEZ policy spent twenty years chasing.
- [India's Demographic Clock — The Deadline Beneath Every Other Debate](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/india-s-demographic-clock/) (11 June 2026, Political Economy): India's median age is 28 and its working-age share peaks in the 2040s. Why the demographic dividend is a deadline for jobs, skills and delivery.
- [Four Codes, Thirty-Six Rulebooks — The Labour Reform That Is Not Yet a Reform](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/four-codes-thirty-six-rulebooks-the-labour-reform-that-is-not-yet-a-reform/) (4 June 2026, Governance & Delivery): Twenty-nine labour laws were repealed in November 2025 and central rules arrived in May 2026. Why the states now decide whether the labour codes work.
- [The Northeast Is Not the Periphery — A Gateway That Is Not Yet Open](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-northeast-india-is-not-the-periphery/) (28 May 2026, Federalism & the Northeast): Over ₹6 lakh crore committed to the Northeast in a decade, yet exports fell from $50.8m to $47.6m. Why the gateway strategy stalls at execution.
- [The Tariff That Was Never Lawful — Negotiate for Durability, Not Relief](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-tariff-that-was-never-lawful-what-india-conceded-and-what-it-learned/) (14 May 2026, Political Economy): India won relief from a 50% US tariff, then the US Supreme Court struck the tariff down. The trade negotiation lesson: price legal durability first.
- [The Specialist Who Was Never Sanctioned](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-specialist-who-was-never-sanctioned/) (10 May 2026, State Capacity): The specialist shortfall at rural community health centres seemed to shrink by a third. The specialists barely moved; the requirement was rewritten.
- [Cities Without Money — The Third Tier and the Capacity It Lacks](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/cities-without-money-the-third-tier-and-the-capacity-it-lacks/) (7 May 2026, State Capacity): Indian cities produce about 60% of GDP and raise 0.6% of it. What the Sixteenth Finance Commission's ₹3.6 lakh crore means for urban local bodies.
- [The Thirty-Nine Percent Question — Health Spending and What It Buys](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-thirty-nine-percent-question-health-spending-and-what-it-buys/) (30 April 2026, Health & Human Development): Out-of-pocket health spending fell from 62.6% to about 39%, while public spending sits at 1.8% of GDP. What India's health money actually buys.
- [Who Regulates the Regulators](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/who-regulates-the-regulators/) (23 April 2026, Institutions & Reform): India built independent regulators for its key sectors, then left their appointments, budgets and accountability inside the ministries they check.
- [Airsheds Do Not Respect District Lines](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/airsheds-do-not-respect-district-lines/) (16 April 2026, Resources & Climate): India measures air pollution by city and manages it by municipality, but smog travels across whole regions. The case for airshed governance in Delhi NCR.
- [The Missing Middle of Indian Enterprise](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-missing-middle-of-indian-enterprise/) (9 April 2026, Political Economy): Only 14% of India's MSMEs have formal credit, against a ₹25-30 lakh crore gap. Why Indian firms stay small, and what would let them scale.
- [The Discom Turnaround — and What It Does Not Yet Prove](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-discom-turnaround-and-what-it-does-not-yet-prove/) (2 April 2026, State Capacity): India's power distributors posted a ₹2,701 crore profit in FY25, the first in over a decade. A turnaround built on conditional money, and its limits.
- [The Aquifer Is the Real Budget Constraint](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-aquifer-is-the-real-budget-constraint/) (26 March 2026, Resources & Climate): India extracts 247 billion cubic metres of groundwater a year, a quarter of the world's total. How power subsidies and procurement drain the aquifer.
- [Five Crore Cases and the Arithmetic of Delay](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/five-crore-cases-and-the-arithmetic-of-delay/) (19 March 2026, Institutions & Reform): India's courts carry 5.05 crore pending cases. Two in five district-court cases are stuck at appearance or service. Where the remedy for delay lies.
- [Citizens Who Move, Entitlements That Do Not](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/citizens-who-move-entitlements-that-do-not/) (12 March 2026, Governance & Delivery): India built a portable ration card and stopped there. Why migrant workers still cannot vote, enrol a child or claim a pension where they live.
- [Sixty-Eight Paise in the Rupee](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/sixty-eight-paise-in-the-rupee/) (8 March 2026, Federalism & the Northeast): Northeastern and Himalayan states draw 68% of revenue receipts from the Centre. The problem is not dependence but the conditions attached to the money.
- [The Half That Does Not Show Up — India's Female Participation Problem](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-half-that-does-not-show-up/) (5 March 2026, Work & Livelihoods): Female labour force participation has reached 40%, but 44% of women outside work cite care duties. Why unpaid care is India's binding constraint.
- [The Title Is the Asset — Why Indian Land Cannot Be Used as Capital](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-title-is-the-asset/) (26 February 2026, Political Economy): India's land titles are presumptive, not conclusive. Fifteen years of digitisation still leave every record rebuttable, and land unusable as capital.
- [Twenty Years After Prakash Singh — The Reform That Was Ordered and Never Delivered](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/twenty-years-after-prakash-singh/) (19 February 2026, State Capacity): The Supreme Court ordered seven police reforms in 2006. Twenty years on, no state fully complies and 5.3 lakh posts stand vacant. What delivery needs.
- [The Country That Stopped Counting Itself](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-country-that-stopped-counting-itself/) (12 February 2026, Institutions & Reform): India's last completed census was in 2011; the next counts to 1 March 2027. What sixteen years on an old denominator did to food security and policy.
- [The Capex Budget and the Capacity to Spend It](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-capex-budget-and-the-capacity-to-spend-it/) (5 February 2026, Political Economy): ₹12.22 lakh crore of capital expenditure, and a Union that missed its own capex target two years running. Why spending capacity, not money, binds.
- [The Largest Thing India Does Well](https://www.pritirajbrahma.in/review/the-largest-thing-india-does-well/) (1 February 2026, Institutions & Reform): India moved 64.2 crore voters through the polls in six weeks. Why the electoral machine is world class, and how rolls, seats and funding must catch up.
